title: Three Odd Values in a Row
statement:
Given an integer array nums, return true if there are three odd numbers at consecutive positions somewhere in it, and false otherwise.

Values may be negative. A negative number such as -3 is odd too.

examples.why: 5, 7 and 9 sit next to each other and are all odd.
There are four odd numbers in total, but an even 2 breaks them into runs of two.
Negative odd numbers count. In JavaScript, -3 % 2 is -1, not 1.

hints: You only care about whether each value is odd. Picture the array as a row of odd/even flags.
Count how many odd numbers you have seen in a row. An even number resets the count.
Return true the moment the count reaches 3. Test oddness with x % 2 !== 0 so negatives work.

explain.intuition:
Walk the array once and keep a streak counter: how many odd numbers in a row end at the current position. An odd value extends the streak, an even value resets it to 0. As soon as the streak reaches 3 you have your answer.

The trap is the oddness test. In JavaScript the remainder keeps the sign of the dividend, so -3 % 2 is -1, and the check x % 2 === 1 misses every negative odd number. Use x % 2 !== 0 or (x & 1) === 1. Python's % always returns a non-negative result for a positive divisor, so the problem does not show up there.
steps: For each x: if x is odd, add 1 to streak; otherwise set streak = 0.
pitfalls: Counting odd numbers in total instead of in a row, which fails the second example.
Testing oddness with x % 2 === 1 in JavaScript, which is false for -3.
Reading nums[i + 2] past the end of the array when checking windows of three.

solutions.title: Check every window of three
solutions.idea: Look at each group of three neighbours and test all three for oddness.

solutions.title: Streak counter
solutions.idea: Count consecutive odd values; an even value resets the count.

followups: Return the length of the longest run of odd numbers.
Return true if some window of k consecutive values holds at least m odd numbers.
